title: Ephesus (Revelation 2:1–7)
hookLine: hard-working, but they've left their first love
last: FEAR NOT, I AM THE FIRST.

cards: A performance review lands on your desk. The first paragraph glows. You work hard.
You don't give up. You've stood up to people who were lying to you. You've kept going when it was tiring, and you haven't fainted.
Then the turn, in one word: nevertheless. That's roughly the shape of the first letter in Revelation, to the church in Ephesus.
The lampstands from Patmos are about to get their mail, seven letters, one by one, and the first goes to a church that, on paper, is doing everything right.

teach.b: First, who's writing: the risen Christ from the vision, who "holdeth the seven stars in his right hand, who walketh in the midst of the seven golden candlesticks." Walking among them.
He knows these churches from the inside.
Second, the praise, and it's real. "I know thy works, and thy labour, and thy patience." They've tested people who claimed to be apostles and found them liars.
They've endured, and "for my name's sake hast laboured, and hast not fainted." Not a lazy church.

teach.h: NEVERTHELESS: THOU HAST LEFT THY FIRST LOVE.
teach.b: Third, the turn: "Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love." Left, not lost. Readers hear the first love more than one way.
Some hear love for Christ himself, the warmth of the early days. Some hear love for one another, which can thin out in a church busy defending the truth. Some hear both, and the text doesn't choose.
In this letter, hard work doesn't count as love on its own. A church can be right, busy and tired, and still have walked away from what started it.

teach.h: REMEMBER, TURN, DO THE FIRST WORKS.
teach.b: Fourth, the way back, in three steps: "Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works." Remember where it began. Repent: turn around.
Do the first works: don't wait to feel it again; do what you did when you loved.
And a promise that reaches back to Eden: "To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of God."

how: Christians read the letters to the seven churches as words to their own congregations, and some churches use the letter to Ephesus in retreats and renewal services that invite members to remember how their faith began.

games.q: you're the church in Ephesus. you've worked hard and stayed faithful, but you're told you've left your first love. what does the letter ask you to do?
o: remember, turn around, and do the first works.
wait until the feeling comes back.
games.why: "Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works." not more effort, and not waiting: doing what you did when you loved.

practice: Think back to the start of something you still do, a faith, a friendship, a marriage, a job, a craft, and let one of its first works come into view: something you did back then, unasked, just because you loved it.
If you pray, bring that memory to God; if not, hold it, and notice how far or how near it feels now.

wordCard.voice: Ephesus. The first of the seven churches: hard-working and enduring, and told it had left its first love, with a way back: remember, turn, do the first works.

carryVoice: Your line: your first love. Left, not lost, so the road back is still open. I'll be here tomorrow.
